lastCompletedStory.title: Make the supervisor the sole writer of story passes:true via a generalized finalizeStory

nextStoryContext: US-003 (ADR 0035, variant A-i) generalized loop.ts's finalize funnel: BOTH a worker 'incomplete' outcome AND a worker 'pass' outcome (worker already wrote+committed passes:true itself) now funnel through the SAME supervisor-side runGates()+finalizeStory() gate before the flip is trusted -- the pass/incomplete distinction collapses for the flip only. Excluded: a 'pass' outcome that merely RE-CONFIRMS a story already passes:true at the top of the SAME iteration (CAM-36 stale-no-op case), discriminated by the existing `alreadyPassingAtTop` check (computed once, reused by both the funnel gate and the no-progress streak counter). When the supervisor's own gate is RED on a 'pass' outcome, it actively REVERTS the worker's premature passes:true back to false via a fresh readPrd+mutate+writePrd (not the stale `prd` var from iteration top), so a false claim never carries forward -- run degrades to 'blocked', not silently trusted. host.ts's finalizeStory is now idempotent: since a 'pass' outcome can mean the worker already committed passes:true, `git add -A` may stage nothing and `git commit` on an empty stage would normally fail ('nothing to commit') -- guarded with `git diff --cached --quiet` (exit 0 = nothing staged) returning ok:true 'already finalized' instead of erroring; proven against a REAL git repo in test/integration/finalize-story-real-git.test.ts (not an injected fake), mirroring the commit-exists-real-git.test.ts precedent. result.ts's readWorkerOutcome was intentionally left untouched (DONE+passes:false already resolves 'incomplete'; the existing red-gate refusal CAM-202 and commit-existence gate remain intact) -- this story is loop.ts+host.ts wiring only. Discovered and worked around a genuine TS control-flow quirk while writing the new tests: a `let x: T | null = null` reassigned ONLY inside a closure passed as a callback narrows to `never` (not `T | null`) at the read site outside the closure -- reproduced directly against this repo's tsc, not project-specific config; fixed by capturing into a `const arr: T[] = []` + `.push()` pattern instead (see patterns.md). Per the story's own notes, land BEFORE US-006 (ACL Write-deny) so the supervisor already owns the flip before the worker loses prd.json write authority -- confirm US-006 has not already regressed this ordering assumption before implementing it.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal supervisor wiring (finalizeStory/loop.ts funnel generalization) and Bun/git/tsc behavior; no external library API surface exercised.
